readings.title: Job Answers Bildad
readings.subtitle: No Contending with El
readings.text: [Job 9:1] And Iyyoḇ answered and said: [2] “Truly I know it is so, but how is man right with <dn>El</dn>? [3] “If he desires to contend with <dn>Him</dn>, <dn>He</dn> does not answer him one of a thousand. [4] “Wise in heart and mighty in power – who has hardened himself against <dn>Him</dn> and was at peace? [5] “<dn>He</dn> removes mountains, and they do not know it, when <dn>He</dn> overturns them in <dn>His</dn> displeasure; [6] “Who shakes the earth out of its place, and its columns tremble; [7] “Who commands the sun, and it does not rise; and <dn>He</dn> seals up the stars; [8] “Stretching out the heavens by <dn>Himself</dn>, and treading upon the waves of the sea; [9] “Making Ash, Kesil, and Kimah, and the rooms of the south; [10] “Doing great deeds, till there is no searching; and wonders till there is no number. [11] “See, <dn>He</dn> goes by me, and I do not see; and <dn>He</dn> moves on, but I do not perceive <dn>Him</dn>. [12] “See, <dn>He</dn> snatches away, who turns <dn>Him</dn> back? Who says to <dn>Him</dn>, ‘What are <dn>You</dn> doing?’ [13] “<dn>Eloah</dn> does not withdraw <dn>His</dn> displeasure; the helpers of Rahaḇ bow beneath <dn>Him</dn>. [14] “How much less when I answer <dn>Him</dn>, choosing my words with <dn>Him</dn>? [15] “For though I were righteous, I would not answer; I would make supplication to my <dn>Judge</dn>. [16] “If I called and <dn>He</dn> answered me, I would not believe that <dn>He</dn> was listening to my voice. [17] “For <dn>He</dn> crushes me with a tempest, and has increased my wounds without cause. [18] “<dn>He</dn> does not allow me to recover my breath, but fills me with bitterness. [19] “If of power, see, <dn>He</dn> is strong! And if of right-ruling, who would appoint me a time? [20] “Though I were righteous, my own mouth would declare me wrong; though perfect, <dn>He</dn> declares me perverse.

readings.title: Job Answers Bildad (Continued)
readings.subtitle: Days Swifter Than a Runner
readings.text: [Job 9:21] “I am perfect! I do not know myself, I despise my life. [22] “It is all one, therefore I say, ‘<dn>He</dn> destroys the perfect and the wrong.’ [23] “If the scourge slays suddenly, <dn>He</dn> mocks at the despair of the innocent. [24] “Earth is given into the hand of the wrong; <dn>He</dn> covers the faces of its judges. If it is not <dn>He</dn>, who else could it be? [25] “And my days are swifter than a runner; they flee away, they shall see no good. [26] “They pass by like swift ships, like an eagle swooping on its prey. [27] “If I say, ‘Let me forget my complaint, let me put off my sad face, and smile,’ [28] “I am afraid of all my sufferings; I know that <dn>You</dn> do not hold me innocent. [29] “If I am to be wrong, why do I labour in vain? [30] “If I wash myself with snow water, and cleanse my hands with soap, [31] “Then <dn>You</dn> dip me in the pit, and my own garments shall abominate me. [32] “For <dn>He</dn> is not a man, as I am, that I should answer <dn>Him</dn>, that we should come together in right-ruling. [33] “There is no mediator between us, who would lay his hand on us both. [34] “Let <dn>Him</dn> take <dn>His</dn> rod away from me, and do not let <dn>His</dn> fear startle me. [35] “Then I would speak and not fear <dn>Him</dn>, but it is not so with me.

readings.title: Job's Plea to Elohim
readings.subtitle: Why Do You Contend With Me?
readings.text: [Job 10:1] “My being is weary of my life; I let loose my complaint, I speak in the bitterness of my being. [2] “I say to <dn>Eloah</dn>, ‘Do not declare me wrong; show me why <dn>You</dn> contend with me. [3] ‘Is it good to <dn>You</dn> that <dn>You</dn> should oppress, that <dn>You</dn> should despise the work of <dn>Your</dn> hands, and shine on the counsel of the wrong? [4] ‘Do <dn>You</dn> have eyes of flesh? Do <dn>You</dn> see as man sees? [5] ‘Are <dn>Your</dn> days like the days of a mortal man? Are <dn>Your</dn> years like the days of a mighty man, [6] ‘That <dn>You</dn> should seek for my crookedness and search out my sin? [7] ‘For <dn>You</dn> know that I am not wrong, and there is no one to deliver from <dn>Your</dn> hand. [8] ‘<dn>Your</dn> hands have made me and shaped me, together all around, yet <dn>You</dn> destroy me. [9] ‘Remember, I pray, that <dn>You</dn> have made me like clay. And would <dn>You</dn> turn me into dust again? [10] ‘Did <dn>You</dn> not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese, [11] ‘Clothe me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews? [12] ‘<dn>You</dn> have granted me life and kindness, and <dn>Your</dn> visitation has preserved my spirit. [13] ‘And these <dn>You</dn> have hidden in <dn>Your</dn> heart; I know that this was with <dn>You</dn>: [14] ‘If I sin, then <dn>You</dn> watch me, and do not acquit me of my crookedness. [15] ‘If I am wrong, woe to me! And if I am righteous, I do not lift up my head – filled with shame and seeing my affliction! [16] ‘If my head is exalted, <dn>You</dn> hunt me like a fierce lion, and again <dn>You</dn> show <dn>Yourself</dn> wonderful against me. [17] ‘<dn>You</dn> renew <dn>Your</dn> witnesses against me, and increase <dn>Your</dn> displeasure toward me; changes and a host are with me. [18] ‘Why then did <dn>You</dn> bring me forth from the womb? I should have breathed my last, and no eye would have seen me. [19] ‘I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave. [20] ‘Are not my days few? Then cease! Leave me alone, that I may smile a little, [21] ‘Before I go, and I do not return, to the land of darkness and the shadow of death, [22] ‘A land as dark as darkness itself, as the shadow of death, without order, and the light is as darkness.’ ”

readings.title: Zophar the Naamathite Speaks
readings.subtitle: Can You Find Out the Deep Things of Elohim?
readings.text: [Job 11:1] Then Tsophar the Na‛amathite answered and said, [2] “Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man of lips be declared right? [3] “Should your empty talk silence men, and you mock, with no one to put you to shame? [4] “For you have said, ‘My teaching is clear, and I am clean in your eyes.’ [5] “But oh, that <dn>Eloah</dn> would speak, and open <dn>His</dn> lips against you, [6] “And show you the secrets of wisdom! For sound wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that <dn>Elohim</dn> forgets some of your crookedness for you. [7] “Would you find out the deep things of <dn>Elohim</dn>? Would you find out the limit of the <dn>Almighty</dn>? [8] “It is high as the heavens, what do you do? Deeper than She’ol, what do you know? [9] “Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea. [10] “If <dn>He</dn> passes by, or shuts up, or calls an assembly, who turns <dn>Him</dn> back? [11] “For <dn>He</dn> knows men of falsehood; and <dn>He</dn> sees wickedness, will <dn>He</dn> not consider it? [12] “For an empty-headed man would get a heart, when a wild donkey’s colt is born a man. [13] “If you would prepare your heart, and stretch out your hands toward <dn>Him</dn>; [14] “If wickedness is in your hand, put it far away, and let no unrighteousness dwell in your tents; [15] “Then, indeed, you would lift up your face without spot, and you would be steadfast, and not fear; [16] “Because you would forget your misery, remember it as waters that have passed away, [17] “And your life would rise brighter than noonday; darkness would be as the morning. [18] “And you would trust, because there is expectation; and you would look around and take your rest in safety. [19] “And you would lie down, with no one to make you afraid, and many would seek your favour. [20] “But the eyes of the wrong do fail, and their refuge shall perish, and their expectation is a breathing out of life!”

readings.title: Job Answers Zophar
readings.subtitle: Wisdom and Power Belong to Him
readings.text: [Job 12:1] And Iyyoḇ answered and said, [2] “Truly you are the people, and wisdom dies with you! [3] “I also have a heart as well as you; I am not inferior to you. And who does not know such as these? [4] “I am one mocked by his friends, who called on <dn>Eloah</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> answered him; the righteous, the perfect one, is mocked. [5] “A lamp is despised in the thought of the one who is at ease, prepared for those whose feet slip. [6] “The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke <dn>El</dn> are safe, to him who brings <dn>Eloah</dn> in his hand. [7] “But now ask the beasts, and they teach you; and the birds of the heavens, and they declare to you; [8] “Or speak to the earth, and it teaches you; and the fish of the sea relate to you. [9] “Who among all these does not know that the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done this? [10] “In whose hand is the life of every living being, and the breath of all mankind? [11] “Does not the ear try words? And the mouth taste food for itself? [12] “Is wisdom with the aged, and understanding in length of days? [13] “With <dn>Him</dn> are wisdom and might, <dn>He</dn> has counsel and understanding. [14] “See, <dn>He</dn> breaks down, and it is not rebuilt; <dn>He</dn> shuts a man in, and it is not opened. [15] “See, <dn>He</dn> withholds the waters, and they dry up; and <dn>He</dn> sends them out, and they overturn the earth. [16] “With <dn>Him</dn> are strength and sound wisdom; the misled and the misleader are <dn>His</dn>. [17] “<dn>He</dn> leads counsellors away stripped, and makes judges go mad. [18] “<dn>He</dn> loosens the bond of sovereigns, and binds a girdle on their loins. [19] “<dn>He</dn> leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty. [20] “<dn>He</dn> turns aside the lip of the trusted ones, and takes away the discernment of the elders. [21] “<dn>He</dn> pours contempt on nobles, and loosens the girdle of the strong. [22] “<dn>He</dn> reveals deep matters out of darkness, and brings the shadow of death to light. [23] “<dn>He</dn> makes nations great, and destroys them; <dn>He</dn> spreads out nations, and leads them out. [24] “<dn>He</dn> turns aside the heart of the chiefs of the people of the earth, and makes them wander in a pathless waste. [25] “They grope in the dark without light, and <dn>He</dn> makes them stagger like a drunkard.
